title: Route account_actions_sheet.dart's Sign Out / Delete Account icon glyphs through a theme token instead of a Colors.white literal
rule: lens:theme-consistency (beyond no_color_literal_outside_theme's Color(0x..) scope; extend lint or document statics-allowed)
why: account_actions_sheet.dart's Sign Out and Delete Account icon glyphs are Colors.white literals, even though the rest of the same file consistently routes color through AppTheme.*/AppColors.*/theme.colorScheme.* (e.g. lines 128,140,152,160,178,188,204,261). an7_destructive_icon_contrast_test.dart pins this literal as the expected value rather than a themed constant, so the AN-7 contrast fix has no named, reusable 'high-contrast-on-errorContainer' token — a future theme edit (e.g. a dark-mode errorContainer swap) has no single place to update and could silently reintroduce an AN-7-class invisible-icon bug elsewhere that reuses the same pattern without the literal.
recommendation: Add a named theme constant (e.g. an AppTheme.onErrorContainer-style token fixed to a contrasting value) and reference it at both call sites instead of the Colors.white literal; update an7_destructive_icon_contrast_test.dart to assert against that constant.
acceptance_criteria: account_actions_sheet.dart's two destructive-icon color values reference a named theme constant, not a Colors.white literal.
`dart run custom_lint` (once its analyzer-version crash is fixed) reports no no_color_literal_outside_theme violation for these two lines.

refutations: Cited rule no_color_literal_outside_theme only fires on Color(0x…) hex-literal constructor calls (packages/custom_lints/lib/src/rules/no_color_literal_outside_theme.dart:71-88: addInstanceCreationExpression, typeName=='Color'). Its own test asserts Colors.white must NOT be flagged ('Named constants
corrections: The 'why' overstates consistency: same file already has untouched Colors.white/grey.shade300/transparent literals at lines 35, 97, 118, so it isn't true that 'the rest of the file consistently routes color through theme tokens' — weakens but doesn't kill the two-site defect claim.

Rule citation is factually wrong: no_color_literal_outside_theme excludes Colors.* named constants by explicit design and unit test. No other coding-standards.md rule bans Colors.white; it's the established app-wide pattern (app_theme.dart onError/onPrimary/etc., and this very file's own line 97 'color: Colors.white').
